requirements_summary: Primary workload: conversational customer support chat + nightly reranking for product search
Target sustained throughput: 30,000 tokens/sec across fleet during normal peaks
Burst capability: short bursts to 120k tokens/sec for 10-15 minutes during promotions
Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 180ms for chat single-turn at 512 token context
Concurrency cap expectations: support 400 concurrent chat sessions with tail-latency safeguards
Model preferences: prefer open LLMs (70B-100B) with quantized vram footprint; fallback to smaller family when needed
Data requirements: VPC private deployment, KMS for keys, audit logs retained 365 days, EU residency for EMEA traffic
negotiation_points: Guaranteed min_tokens_per_sec: customer asks for 30k sustained tokens/sec guaranteed
Concurrency guarantees: explicit cap of 400 concurrent chat sessions / route; Redwood proposes elastic concurrency with headroom
Burst policy: define 3-tier burst windows (30s, 10min, 1hr) with defined allowed oversubscription and throttle behavior
Warm-up/Warm-cache: POC to validate prefix/KV cache warm-up times; proposal includes prefetch warmers
Overage pricing: Skyward wants clear per-token overage rate and crediting for missed SLOs
SLA penalties: customer requests uptime + performance SLA (credits) tied to 95th tail latency and sustained throughput
Reserved GPU mapping: detailed GPU count + model mapping required for contract; Redwood to provide mapping table and failover plan
Fallback routing: explicit fallback policy to smaller model family with quality delta thresholds (acceptable failure modes)
po_terms_summary: Customer prefers annual committed capacity with quarterly review. Wants 30-day termination right for material SLA failures. Seeks detailed capacity-to-GPU mapping, committed burst credits, and three-month ramp schedule.
notes:
